hypothesis: The neuron responds selectively to a prominent, continuous vertical dark line, bar, or elongated structure set against a lighter, low-contrast background. The activating feature is consistently a dark charcoal, black, or deep grey linear element—such as a vertical pole, wire, notebook spine, deep shadow cleft, door gap, or expansion joint—that serves as a strong vertical axis within the composition. This element typically spans 50–100% of the image height while remaining relatively slender (roughly 5–15% of the image width) and is centered or slightly off-center. The neuron remains invariant to the semantic identity of the vertical form (whether biological, architectural, or mechanical) and its surface texture, as long as the stark dark-on-light contrast and strictly vertical orientation are preserved against a background of pale grey, off-white, or beige.
